points.t: Crops of yellow pustules and brown dots on the palms or soles, or thick, fissured, sharply bordered plaques.
Neutrophilic inflammation (IL-36/IL-17); smoking is the main modifiable trigger for PPP.
Stop smoking, very potent topical steroid (± occlusion), emollients, then specialist phototherapy, acitretin or biologics (NICE CG153 for psoriasis).
Generalised pustular psoriasis (emergency), tinea pedis with pustules, and pompholyx.

points: trauma/friction (Koebner — manual work), infection, stress, lithium, β-blockers, smoking, alcohol, obesity.
crops of 1–10 mm yellow pustules on thenar/hypothenar eminences, central palms, insteps, heels → dry to **brown "rusty" macules**; scale, fissures; burning/pain > itch; symmetrical.
clinical; swab (sterile) and scrapings to exclude infection/tinea if unilateral.

items.t: Fever with sheets of pustules beyond the hands and feet: **generalised pustular psoriasis**, emergency.
Inability to work or walk: early dermatology referral.
Pustules on one foot only, or with interdigital scale: scrape for **tinea**.

pearls.t: Smoking cessation is the single most effective change in PPP; offer stop-smoking support at every visit.
Use very potent steroids under cling-film or cotton-glove occlusion at night for short periods, then step down.
Tell patients the pustules are **sterile**: antibiotics do not help.
Screen for psoriatic arthritis (PEST) and ask about chest-wall pain (SAPHO).
